clue.text: Even given the apartment number

parts.note: an apartment is a flat in British English
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone is being fair by supplying the number of the apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adjective or adverb but is the verb: to make level.
explanation.definitionFit: To even a surface is to make it level and smooth, the verb sense.

clue.text: Skinhead pursuing a country girl

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this letter follows the country

parts.note: France is a country
the head, or first letter, of skin is S

explanation.surface: A skinhead chases a girl from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' suggests a thug, but read as skin's head it is just its first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances is a female given name, so a girl may be called it.

clue.text: Carpeting with cross laid in a cathedral

indicators.note: laid in means placed inside, so the cross goes within the words a cathedral

parts.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, as in York Minster
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A carpet with a cross design has been laid in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town famous for its woven carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of machine-woven pile carpet, named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Nervous, though it's quite possibly perfect

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious even though everything is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is the grammatical perfect, a verb tense, as in 'I have eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous people are strained and tightly wound; and the perfect is one grammatical tense among several.

clue.text: Critically discriminating as tune is rendered

indicators.note: a tune that is rendered is performed in a new version, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone judges a musical performance with a critic's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare word: nasute means keen-scented, hence shrewd or discerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasute literally means keen-nosed, and by extension describes someone with a sharp, discerning judgement.

clue.text: The shoot occupied by an object in the sky — a bird

indicators.note: occupied by means another piece takes up the space inside this word

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot of a plant
a star is an object seen in the night sky

explanation.surface: Someone notices a bird and some flying object up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The bustard is a large ground-dwelling bird of open country.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large heavy game bird of grassland and steppe.

clue.text: Everybody's into bonuses — they give people a lift

indicators.note: into means the word for everybody goes inside the word for bonuses

parts.note: boons are blessings or welcome extras, like bonuses
everybody is all; the 's here stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Everyone is keen on bonuses, which cheer people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give people a lift' sounds like cheering up, but here it means literally carrying them aloft, as hot-air craft do.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-air craft carry passengers upwards, literally raising them into the air.

clue.text: Such building material sets, and no mistake!

indicators.note: and no mistake is an emphatic phrase, but mistake here signals the preceding letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A building material definitely sets hard, no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and no mistake' reads as emphasis; only 'mistake' is the signal, rearranging SETSANDNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock widely quarried for building walls and houses.

clue.text: Short article one's read on the French passage

parts.note: a is the short indefinite article
one is I, and the 's stands for 'is', giving I plus S
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone reads a brief French article about a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read on' simply places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Return is nil in the small department store

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters sit inside the short form of department

parts.note: dept is the short form of department

indicators.note: return means the words is and nil are read backwards together

parts.note: nil is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A department store reports zero takings in its small section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns both words together, making OSI. The surface's 'department store' looks like one shop, but 'store' splits off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a stock or accumulated reserve, such as a mineral bed or a sum kept in a bank.

clue.text: Sound colonels, but nuts!

parts.note: colonels said aloud is kernels, and these particular kernels are a well-known edible variety

explanation.surface: Some army officers seem sane yet are actually crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' pretends to mean sane, then 'nuts' pretends to mean mad; really colonel and kernel sound alike, and the kernels are nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are oval nut kernels from a tree related to the peach.

clue.text: Queues to go inside and drink

parts.note: to line something is to cover its inside, as a lining goes inside a coat
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: People queue to enter a pub for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queues' is a verb here: forms a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To line up is to stand one behind another in a queue.

clue.text: Perversity in countesses not to be trifled with

indicators.note: something trifled with is played about, so the letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Aristocratic ladies who must not be toyed with display a contrary streak.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all fifteen letters of 'in countesses not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perversity is a wilful tendency to argue and quarrel, which is a quarrelsome nature.

clue.text: South American solicitor stayed till the end

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in that literal sense

explanation.surface: A South American lawyer remained to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits business: a tout, a pushy salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out a show is to remain until it has finished.

clue.text: On the wrong track, as climbers could well be

explanation.surface: Mountaineers might lose their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the pole' is British slang for mistaken or confused; climbing plants, and climbers of the human sort, go up poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means confused or mistaken; and climbing plants grow along a supporting stake.

clue.text: Saucy lines, not ill-written

indicators.note: ill-written means badly set down, so the letters of the words before are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some cheeky lines were nonetheless well written.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means cheeky or impertinent, showing rude disrespect.

clue.text: Deter taxi misuse — hand over the offender

indicators.note: misuse signals the letters of the preceding words are used wrongly, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning sign urges people not to misuse taxis and to hand in offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to surrender an accused person to another state for trial.

clue.text: Nurse and others put in custody again!

parts.note: to nurse or bring up young is to rear them
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A nurse and colleagues are locked up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is a verb here: to bring up, raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrest someone is to detain them a second time.

clue.text: Having support, showed off

explanation.surface: Someone with backing paraded proudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A strutted frame is braced with props; and to have walked with a swagger is to have shown off.

clue.text: Fish photographer?

explanation.surface: Is that a photographer of fish?
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is a tropical sea fish; and someone taking snaps is a press cameraman.

clue.text: Some basset, terrier or other dog

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog lover lists breeds: a basset, a terrier, or some other.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gundog breed, one more alongside the basset and terrier.

clue.text: A particular estimation

explanation.surface: An estimate given is quite specific.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is as in 'in every respect': a particular point or detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a detail or aspect; and it also means esteem or high regard.

clue.text: The key is left also

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone says the important thing is that it was left as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not the main point but a cay, a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a low offshore islet or reef, as in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: A situation involving questionable direction

parts.note: a place where several roads meet and the way ahead is in doubt, figuratively a point of decision

explanation.surface: Someone describes a position where the right way is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a critical moment of decision, literally a road junction where several routes meet.

clue.text: Bound to draw from a newspaper leader

parts.note: to tap a barrel is to draw liquid from it
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to take ideas from a newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests obliged; here it means tied up. 'leader' looks like an editorial but is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taped is bound or fastened with adhesive strip.

clue.text: Sets up the right listening equipment

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: Someone installs the correct audio gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening equipment' suggests headphones, but it is the body's own ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear something is to raise it upright, such as a structure.

clue.text: The descendant of brave forebears

parts.note: brave is a Native American warrior, and the descendant is the infant of such a parent

explanation.surface: Someone praises the offspring of courageous ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective meaning courageous; it is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American baby or young child, so the offspring of a warrior.

clue.text: A few take a cereal from sheer greed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'A few take a cereal from sheer greed' (7): A + ? + A + RICE needs a V, and no reading of 'few' gives it; likely a misprint (perhaps 'five'), not confirmed by any source.
annotationWithheld.clue: A few take a cereal from sheer greed

clue.text: Plainly most embarrassed about a minister set wrong

parts.note: re means about or concerning
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a title held by a minister of religion

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of set are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone is most visibly ashamed about a clergyman being ordered badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment shows as blushing, so the person most visibly flushed is the one with the deepest blush.

clue.text: A point will be seen in due course

indicators.note: will be seen in means the point appears inside the word for due

parts.note: a desert is what someone deserves, their due, as in just deserts
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A point will become clear eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in due course' reads as eventually; it splits so 'course' is the definition. 'due' is the noun, as in getting one's just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.
